stories.headline: Did the Water Board Really Double Its Tariff? Tracing a Viral Claim to Its Source
stories.summary: A widely shared post says a regional water board doubled household rates this quarter. The board's own tariff schedule shows a smaller change, and the post traces back to a misread table.
body: At first glance the claim is simple: rates doubled. The post that started it carries a screenshot of a table with two columns of numbers, and the larger column is roughly twice the smaller one.

Joan pulled the board's published tariff schedule and found that the screenshot mixes two different things. One column is the base rate per cubic meter. The other is the base rate plus the fixed infrastructure charge, which the board has listed separately for years.

The base rate did rise. The size of the rise depends on which consumption band a household sits in, and the board's own notice gives the percentage for each band. None of them reaches one hundred percent.

Two paid research lookups were used to check whether the post was copied from an earlier claim. Both found the same screenshot circulating a week before the board's notice was published, which points to a misread of an older document.
know: The board published a revised tariff schedule dated 3 November.
The base rate rose in every consumption band, by amounts between 6 and 19 percent in the published notice.
The screenshot in the viral post combines base rate and fixed charge in one column.
The earliest copy of the screenshot found predates the board's notice.
unclear: Whether the fixed infrastructure charge is also scheduled to change next quarter.
Who first posted the screenshot. Three accounts share it with identical captions.
Whether any households were billed under a transitional rate not covered by the notice.

confidence.reason: The claim traces to a primary document, and the discrepancy is explained by two independent checks.

stories.headline: Battery Pack Recall Rumor: One Manufacturer Notice, Three Retellings
stories.summary: Posts say a portable battery brand recalled every unit sold this year. The only notice found covers one production batch, and the larger claim has no origin.
body: The rumor arrived in three forms. One said all units were recalled, one said all units from the last twelve months, and one said only units with a specific model code.
The manufacturer's safety page lists a single notice. It names one production batch by serial range and asks owners to stop using affected packs and contact support.
Joan bought two research lookups to find who first widened the claim. The broader versions appear to descend from a forum thread that quoted the notice and then added a sentence of its own.
A tip from a verified human, who owns an affected unit, confirmed the serial range printed on the label matches the notice. The tip did not speak to how many units exist in that range.
know: The manufacturer posted one safety notice covering a single production batch.
The notice gives a serial range and a support contact.
A verified owner confirmed that their unit's serial number falls inside the range.
unclear: How many units fall inside the affected batch.
Whether other batches share the same component supplier.
Whether any regulator has opened a review.

sources.label: Forum thread that widened the claim

confidence.reason: The narrow recall is confirmed by the manufacturer. The size of the batch and any wider risk are not documented.

stories.headline: A Funding Announcement for an Open Source Library, Checked Line by Line
stories.summary: A press post says a foundation committed a large sum to a popular library. The foundation's own page lists a smaller grant and a different recipient name.
body: The announcement reads cleanly: a foundation, a library, and a figure with many zeros. Each sentence is plausible. The trouble is that no sentence links to anything.
Joan searched the foundation's grant register and found one entry that matches the library's maintainers by name. The amount is a fraction of the announced figure and is spread across two years.
The larger number appears to come from the total of the foundation's whole cycle, which includes grants to other recipients. The announcement may have folded the two together.
The maintainers have not answered a request for comment. That absence is recorded here and is not treated as confirmation or denial.
know: The foundation's grant register lists one matching entry, smaller than the announced figure.
The grant is paid over two years.
The larger figure matches the foundation's total for the whole cycle.
unclear: Whether a second grant is pending approval.
Whether the recipient name difference reflects a legal entity or a mistake.
What the maintainers intend to say about the discrepancy.

confidence.reason: Only one primary document was found and the maintainers did not respond. The explanation for the larger figure is an inference.
